messages:
maya: Heads-up — I see a perf regression after the kernel-heuristic tweak from yesterday. nsys + perfetto traces point to an extra prefetch kernel launch on tiny batches that serializes the queue and spikes tail latency (~4-6ms per request).

liam: yikes. same in staging? saw a 95p jump earlier but thought it was noise.

maya: yes staging + canary. spike correlates with batch_size <= 2 and low KV-cache hit rate. timeline snippet: prefetch memcpy -> small compute kernel -> idle -> big matmul.

sasha: pasted a short nsys timeline excerpt I grabbed:
```
GPU activities:
  memcpy_h2d  [0.4ms]
  kernel prefetch_small  [1.1ms]
  kernel launch_overhead  [0.6ms]
  kernel matmul_main    [8.2ms]
```
You can see the prefetch launch splits the batch window.

nsys-bot: nsys run available: https://perf.ns/runs/0x9ab2 (staging-2026-03-15) :mag_right:

liam: hypothesis: the heuristic change now chooses prefetch when any kv_miss > 0 rather than when predicted_prefix_length >= prefetch_window. for tiny batches that causes an unnecessary kernel and synchronization.

maya: agreed. quick fix options: revert heuristic, or add min_batch_threshold (e.g. >=4) before inserting prefetch kernel. also consider async prefetch path that doesn't force stream sync.

sasha: I ran an ablation on the microbench:
- baseline (old heuristic): p95 = 22.1ms
- new heuristic (no guard): p95 = 78.3ms
- new heuristic + min_batch_threshold=4: p95 = 24.7ms
So adding the threshold gives back the perf without losing prefetch benefits on larger batches.

maya: can you share the exact cmd you used for the nsys capture? will try to reproduce locally.

sasha: sure:
```bash
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=tmp/staging-prefetch --sample=none \
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- python -u run_microbench.py --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8
```
Also used perfetto for a longer end-to-end trace to see host scheduling. Perfetto shows a host thread waiting ~3.6ms between enqueue and kernel-launch for the tiny-batch case.

liam: sounds like two issues: (1) kernel selection heuristic too eager, (2) host launch overhead becomes visible when kernel is tiny. both doable: patch heuristic + prefer coalesced prefetch path that keeps data staged on device.

maya: rollout plan: sasha can send a small PR to add min_batch_threshold configurable via runtime flags (default 4). we can enable canary 10% on dedicated and monitor metrics: queue_time_95p, prefetch_launch_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate.

sasha: PR ready, test vectors + nsys trace attached in PR description. link: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/5234

perf-bot: Canary scheduled: dedicated-cluster-3 @ 10% for 30m. Observability alerts: queue_time_95p > 40ms will auto-rollback.

liam: also adding a lightweight metric: prefetch_launches_by_batch_size (counter) so we can see distribution — will push telemetry change now.

maya: perfect. after canary we should run a targeted perfetto capture on the canary traffic and compare host enqueue->launch histograms vs baseline. thanks all :thumbsup:

sasha: noted, I'll collect the canary traces and attach to the ticket.

liam: one more note — add a unit test that simulates kv_miss with batch_size=1 to prevent future regressions.

maya: agreed, add test and a changelog entry under runtime/heuristics.

sasha: will do.
